subject: DI02000171

title.en: Fundamentals of Alternating Voltage and Current

h.en: AC and DC:compare the complete system
h.gu: AC તથા DC:સંપૂર્ણ System Compare કરો

body.en:
Understand the idea

DCnormally has one polarity;ACreverses polarity periodically.A sinusoidal ACsystem is a specific ACcase,not the definition of every possible waveform.

Explanation and application

  • Compare source,voltage conversion,transmission,storage and end-use.ACcan be transformed readily at suitable frequency;ordinary transformers do not operate on steady DC.
  • Batteries store energy chemically and supply DC;rectifiers convert ACto DCand inverters synthesize ACfrom DC,with losses and control requirements.
  • ACsupports established distribution networks and rotating-field machines;DCis useful for electronics,storage and some long-distance links.Neither is universally superior in every application.
  • RMSvalue compares heating in a resistance,not waveform shape or shock safety.Both ACand DCcan be hazardous;the syllabus mains-rated equipment is for supervised laboratory work.
Why is sine average sometimes zero?

Signed full-cycle average is0;positive-half/rectified average is2Xm/π.These are different averaging definitions.
body.gu:
વિચાર સમજીએ

DCમાં સામાન્ય રીતે એક polarityરહે છે;ACમાં polarityperiodicallyબદલાય છે.SinusoidalACએACનો specificcaseછે;દરેક waveformની definitionનહિ.

સમજણ અને ઉપયોગ

  • Source,voltageconversion,transmission,storage/end-usecompareકરો.યોગ્યfrequencyએACનેtransformકરીશકાય;ordinarytransformersteadyDCપરકામનકરે.
  • Batterieschemicallyenergyસંગ્રહે અનેDCઆપે;rectifiersACથીDCતથાinvertersDCથીACબનાવે.Losses/controlrequirementsહોય છે.
  • ACdistributionnetworks/rotating-fieldmachinesમાંઉપયોગી;DCelectronics,storage/કેટલીકlong-distancelinksમાંઉપયોગી.દરેકapplicationમાંએકજuniversallyશ્રેષ્ઠનથી.
  • RMSથીresistanceમાંheatingcompareથાય,waveformshapeકેshocksafetyનહિ.AC/DCબંનેજોખમીહોઈશકે.Syllabusનુંmains-ratedequipmentફક્તsupervisedlabમાટે છે.
Sine Average ક્યારેક Zero કેમ?

Signedfull-cycleaverage0;positive-half/rectifiedaverage2Xm/πછે.બંનેdefinitionsજુદીછે.

body.en:
Understand the idea

Alternating EMFis obtained when the flux linkage of a circuit changes periodically.

Explanation and application

  • EMFmay be induced by motion through a magnetic field or by a time-varying flux linking a stationary winding.The illustrated elementary generator uses relative mechanical rotation.
  • Construction:a magnetic field supplies flux;a coil has Nturns and area A;a shaft changes its angle;slip rings and brushes transfer alternating coil voltage to stationary terminals.
  • For a uniform field and constant angular speed,flux linkage λ=NBAcosθand θ=ωt.Faraday’s law gives e=−dλ/dt=NBAωsinωt.
  • When the coil normal is parallel to the field,flux linkage is maximum but its rate of change is zero.After a quarter turn,flux is zero and EMFmagnitude maximum.
  • After a half turn,the EMFpolarity reverses.A full revolution of this two-pole elementary model gives one electrical cycle;multi-pole machines have more electrical cycles per mechanical turn.

Understand the idea

A waveform is the time plot of a quantity;a cycle is one complete repetition,and its duration is the period T.

Explanation and application

  • Frequency fcounts cycles per second and is measured in hertz: f=1/T.Angular frequency ω=2πfhas units rad/s;one cycle is2πrad or360°.
  • Amplitude is the peak excursion from the chosen reference.For a zero-centred sinusoid,peak-to-peak value is twice amplitude.ADCoffset changes the reference.
  • Equivalent time forms include v=Vm sinωt,Vm sin(2πft),Vm sin(2πt/T)and Vm cos(ωt−90°).Do not mix degrees with rad/s inside a calculation.
  • Unless explicitly stated,these notes use sine-reference time waveforms and RMSphasor magnitudes.Adiagram may choose current or voltage as its labelled reference;phase differences do not change under a common rotation.

Given and assumptions

v=100sin(314.159t+30°)V;the phase offset is expressed in degrees separately.

Step-by-step solution

  1. ω=314.159rad/s≈2π×50;f≈50Hz;T≈0.020s=20ms;amplitude100V.
  2. Write consistently as100sin(2π·50t+π/6)with all angles in radians,or100sin(360·50t+30°)with a degree-mode argument.
  3. At t=0,the instantaneous value is100sin30°=50V;the amplitude remains100V,not50V.

Interpretation and check

Aphase offset does not change frequency or amplitude.
body.gu:
આપેલી માહિતી અને ધારણાઓ

v=100sin(314.159t+30°)V;the phase offset is expressed in degrees separately.

ક્રમબદ્ધ ઉકેલ

  1. ω=314.159rad/s≈2π×50;f≈50Hz;T≈0.020s=20ms;amplitude100V.
  2. બધાanglesradiansમાં100sin(2π·50t+π/6)લખો,અથવાdegree-modeમાં100sin(360·50t+30°)લખો.
  3. t=0પરinstantaneousvalue100sin30°=50Vછે.Amplitude100Vજછે,50Vનહિ.

અર્થ અને ચકાસણી

Phaseoffsetfrequency/amplitudeબદલતું નથી.

body.en:
Understand the idea

Instantaneous value is the value at a particular time;peak is the largest magnitude;RMSis defined by mean-square heating equivalence.

Explanation and application

  • The general RMSdefinition is Xrms=√[(1/T)∫₀ᵀx²dt].Aresistor dissipates the same average heat from a DCvalue equal to the ACcurrent RMS.
  • For a zero-centred sine,Xrms=Xm/√2≈0.7071Xm.The signed average over a complete cycle is0;the positive half-cycle average or rectified average is2Xm/π≈0.6366Xm.
  • Derivation:sin²θ=(1−cos2θ)/2has full-cycle mean1/2,so RMS=Xm/√2.The integral of sinθover0toπis2,giving the half-cycle mean2Xm/π.
  • Peak factor=Xm/Xrms=√2;form factor=Xrms/Xrect.avg=π/(2√2)≈1.1107for a sine.Do not divide by the zero signed full-cycle average.
  • These fixed factors do not apply to arbitrary distorted waveforms.Atrue-RMSmeter still has bandwidth,crest-factor and range limits;an average-responding sine-calibrated meter can misread nonsinusoidal input.

Given and assumptions

Zero-centred sine with Vm=20V.

Step-by-step solution

  1. Vrms=20/√2=14.1421V;positive half-cycle average=40/π=12.7324V.
  2. Signed full-cycle mean=0V;Vpp=40V;peak factor=1.4142;form factor=1.1107.
  3. Across R=10Ω,Irms=1.41421Aand P=Vrms²/R=20W(calculation only).

Interpretation and check

The different values describe the same waveform;they are not interchangeable meter readings.
body.gu:
આપેલી માહિતી અને ધારણાઓ

Zero-centred sine with Vm=20V.

ક્રમબદ્ધ ઉકેલ

  1. Vrms=20/√2=14.1421V;positive half-cycle average=40/π=12.7324V.
  2. Signed full-cycle mean=0V;Vpp=40V;peak factor=1.4142;form factor=1.1107.
  3. Across R=10Ω,Irms=1.41421Aand P=Vrms²/R=20W(calculation only).

અર્થ અને ચકાસણી

અલગvaluesએજwaveformનેવર્ણવે છે;meterreadingsinterchangeableનથી.

body.en:
Understand the idea

Phase difference compares corresponding points of two same-frequency periodic quantities.

Explanation and application

  • For x=Xm sin(ωt+θx),y=Ym sin(ωt+θy),xleads yby θx−θywhen that signed difference is positive in the chosen convention.
  • Time displacement Δtcorresponds to angle|φ|=360°·|Δt|/T=ω|Δt|radians.Aleading sine reaches the corresponding positive-going crossing earlier.
  • At50Hz,a2msdisplacement is36°.Decide lead/lag from the order of like crossings,not merely from a positive magnitude on a calculator.
  • Different frequencies do not have a fixed phase difference over time.For φ=0they are in phase;180°means opposite phase at the same frequency.

Understand the idea

Aphasor encodes magnitude and phase of a steady-state sinusoid at one specified frequency;time variation is implicit.

Explanation and application

  • With the notes’ sine reference,v=√2Vsin(ωt+θ)corresponds to RMSphasor V∠θ.Peak and RMSphasors differ by√2;never combine them without conversion.
  • The positive real axis is the chosen zero-phase reference;counterclockwise angles are positive.Aphasor diagram is not a plot of voltage versus time.
  • Under the exp(jωt)convention,differentiation corresponds to multiplication by jωand integration to division by jω.This explains ideal inductive/capacitive impedance signs.

Understand the idea

Only same-frequency compatible phasors can be added by this steady-state method.

Explanation and application

  • Graphical method:select one scale,draw the first vector,place the second tail at the first head,then draw the resultant from the first tail to the last head.
  • Aparallelogram gives the same resultant for two vectors.Keep reference angle,units and scale visible;drawing precision limits numerical accuracy.
  • Analytical method:resolve each into real and imaginary components,add those components separately,then convert the sum back to magnitude and angle.
  • Example:3∠0°+4∠90°=3+j4=5∠53.1301°,not7∠90°.Scalar addition is valid only for collinear compatible quantities with correct signs.

Understand the idea

Rectangular form x+jymakes addition easy;polar form r∠θmakes multiplication/division easy.

Explanation and application

  • r=√(x²+y²)and θ=atan2(y,x).The ordinary arctan(y/x)alone can give the wrong quadrant or fail when x=0.
  • x=r cosθand y=r sinθ;r≥0.Angles differing by360°represent the same nonzero phasor;the zero phasor has no unique angle.
  • Example:−3+j4=5∠126.8699°;−j5=5∠−90°.Check the signs of both components after conversion.

Understand the idea

Use j²=−1;jrotates a phasor counterclockwise90°.The complex conjugate reverses its angle.

Explanation and application

  • Add/subtract rectangular components: (a+jb)±(c+jd)=(a±c)+j(b±d).
  • Multiply polar magnitudes and add angles;divide magnitudes and subtract angles.Division by a zero phasor is undefined.
  • In rectangular division,multiply numerator/denominator by the denominator’s conjugate.Complex power later uses I*,not Iwithout conjugation.

Given and assumptions

A=3+j4=5∠53.1301°;B=4−j3=5∠−36.8699°.

Step-by-step solution

  1. AB=(3+j4)(4−j3)=24+j7=25∠16.2602°.
  2. A/B=[(3+j4)(4+j3)]/25=j;polar quotient=1∠90°.
  3. Check B·j=3+j4and|AB|=|A||B|=25.

Interpretation and check

A90°rotation is multiplication by j,not adding90to the magnitude.

Understand the idea

Separate given data,reference conventions,formula substitution and physical checks.

Explanation and application

  • Identify waveform and frequency;convert ms,mHandµFto SIunits before substitution.State whether a voltage/current is peak,RMSor instantaneous.
  • Choose an explicit phase reference and keep degree/radian mode consistent.Phasor addition requires rectangular form,not adding magnitudes.
  • Check dimensions,quadrant and limiting cases;convert the final phasor back to a time-domain sine when asked.Report reasonable significant figures.

Given and assumptions

v=24√2sin(100πt)V;i=2√2sin(100πt−π/6)A.

Step-by-step solution

  1. V=24V RMS;I=2A RMS;Vm=33.9411V;Im=2.8284A;f=50Hz;T=20ms.
  2. Vphasor=24∠0°;Iphasor=2∠−30°;current lags voltage30°;time lag=1.66667ms.
  3. At t=0:v=0V;i=−1.41421A.Negative instantaneous current is consistent with a lagging sinusoid.

Interpretation and check

This calculation is a mathematical waveform example,not recorded laboratory data.

આપેલી માહિતી અને ધારણાઓ

v=24√2sin(100πt)V;i=2√2sin(100πt−π/6)A.

ક્રમબદ્ધ ઉકેલ

  1. V=24V RMS;I=2A RMS;Vm=33.9411V;Im=2.8284A;f=50Hz;T=20ms.
  2. Vphasor=24∠0°;Iphasor=2∠−30°;current lags voltage30°;time lag=1.66667ms.
  3. At t=0:v=0V;i=−1.41421A.Negative instantaneous current is consistent with a lagging sinusoid.

અર્થ અને ચકાસણી

આmathematicalwaveformexampleછે;recordedlaboratorydataનહિ.

body.en:
Aim and instruments

Observe sine,square and triangular time waveforms with a CRO/function generator.

Instrument selection

  • Use the approved circuit-specific instruments:generator/CROfor waveform work;isolated source,rated load and appropriate ACV/I/real-power instruments for power circuits.Check manual,ranges,leads and component ratings.
  • The source lists mains-rated variacs/banks;these are supervised laboratory resources,not student DIYinstructions.Avariac does not provide isolation.

Connections and model

Use a low-voltage function-generator output and CRO/DSOwith an approved common return;no mains or three-phase circuit is involved.

Procedure

  1. Check the instrument input limits,set a modest permitted amplitude and zero offset,and select a stable frequency.
  2. Connect signal and common as approved;select coupling/probe/termination settings and trigger from the signal.Adjust time and voltage scales to show complete cycles.
  3. Display each waveform,record shape,period and peak-to-peak excursion,and distinguish a waveform change from a frequency change.
  4. Keep actual readings,supply condition,instrument ranges and uncertainty separate from the computed expected reference.
  5. On a discrepancy,stop and check de-energised connections,model assumptions and instrument suitability;do not increase voltage to force agreement.
  6. After approved shutdown,verify safe capacitor discharge and leave the trainer in its required state.Report only work genuinely performed.

Expected calculations and interpretation

Sine-RMSfactors cannot be copied to square/triangular waves without their own definition and duty/offset assumptions.

Safe fault finding

Unstable display:check trigger,ground reference and timebase before changing the source;unexpected amplitude:check50Ωversus high-impedance termination settings.

Essential precautions

  • Only qualified-supervised energised power-lab work is intended.Never defeat protective earth,connect ammeters across the supply,short phases or change wiring while energised.
  • Scope grounds may be common and earth-referenced.Use approved differential/isolated measurement equipment where needed;never float a mains scope by removing its earth.

body.en:
Aim and instruments

Measure waveform dimensions and derive the specified sine quantities.

Instrument selection

  • Use the approved circuit-specific instruments:generator/CROfor waveform work;isolated source,rated load and appropriate ACV/I/real-power instruments for power circuits.Check manual,ranges,leads and component ratings.
  • The source lists mains-rated variacs/banks;these are supervised laboratory resources,not student DIYinstructions.Avariac does not provide isolation.

Connections and model

Use the same low-voltage generator/CROsetup with calibrated scales and known probe factor.Agrounded scope return must not be moved to an arbitrary live node.

Procedure

  1. Confirm a clean zero-centred sine and note AC/DCcoupling,volts/div,time/div and attenuation settings.
  2. Count vertical peak-to-peak divisions and horizontal divisions per complete cycle;use several cycles to reduce reading uncertainty.
  3. Compute Vpp,Vm,Vrms,T,fand compare available meter/cursor results while retaining uncertainty.Do not multiply the probe factor twice if already configured.
  4. Keep actual readings,supply condition,instrument ranges and uncertainty separate from the computed expected reference.
  5. On a discrepancy,stop and check de-energised connections,model assumptions and instrument suitability;do not increase voltage to force agreement.
  6. After approved shutdown,verify safe capacitor discharge and leave the trainer in its required state.Report only work genuinely performed.

Expected calculations and interpretation

Calculated example only:4divisions at2V/div→Vpp8V,Vm4V,Vrms2.82843V;4divisions at5ms/div→T20ms,f50Hz.

Safe fault finding

Wrong RMSusually means non-sine shape,DCoffset,wrong scale or probe factor.Afull-wave rectified mean is not an RMSreading.

Essential precautions

  • Only qualified-supervised energised power-lab work is intended.Never defeat protective earth,connect ammeters across the supply,short phases or change wiring while energised.
  • Scope grounds may be common and earth-referenced.Use approved differential/isolated measurement equipment where needed;never float a mains scope by removing its earth.

Suggested project plan,not completed experiment evidence.

Explanation and application

  • Build only an instructor-approved low-energy model:magnetic poles,rotating coil/relative motion,identified output terminals and guarded moving parts;use safe sensing,not a mains-driven improvised alternator.
  • Explain λ=NBAcosθand e=NBAωsinθ,then compare predicted phase/shape with genuine observations if performed.Aslip-ring ACmodel differs from a commutator DCmodel.

title.en: Project.7 Chart of alternating voltage generation

body.en:
Understand the idea

Suggested project plan,not completed experiment evidence.

Explanation and application

  • Link four rotation positions to flux linkage and induced EMF;show maximum flux at zero EMFand zero flux at peak EMF.
  • Label coil normal,field direction,angular speed and Faraday’s sign;the chart is an original conceptual illustration,not a photo of completed work.

Understand the idea

Suggested project plan,not completed experiment evidence.

Explanation and application

  • Draw two same-frequency sinusoids and phasors for in-phase,leading,lagging and opposition cases using a stated reference.
  • For a50Hzcase,mark20msper cycle and2ms=36°;use corresponding zero crossings to determine which quantity leads.

Understand the idea

Suggested project plan,not completed experiment evidence.

Explanation and application

  • Select one syllabus concept such as rotating phasor addition or variable-frequency resonance and define the expected measurable relation before building.
  • Prefer paper/mechanical or approved isolated low-voltage models;provide component/range limits and independent calculations.If simulation is used,label it simulation,not physical evidence.

Explain λ=NBAcosθand e=NBAωsinθ,then compare predicted phase/shape with genuine observations if performed.Aslip-ring ACmodel differs from a commutator DCmodel. Calculated ideal example:N100,B0.1T,A0.01m²,f10Hz→Vm6.28319V,Vrms4.44288V;actual loading and field nonuniformity change the result.

Link four rotation positions to flux linkage and induced EMF;show maximum flux at zero EMFand zero flux at peak EMF. Label coil normal,field direction,angular speed and Faraday’s sign;the chart is an original conceptual illustration,not a photo of completed work.

Draw two same-frequency sinusoids and phasors for in-phase,leading,lagging and opposition cases using a stated reference. For a50Hzcase,mark20msper cycle and2ms=36°;use corresponding zero crossings to determine which quantity leads.

Select one syllabus concept such as rotating phasor addition or variable-frequency resonance and define the expected measurable relation before building. Prefer paper/mechanical or approved isolated low-voltage models;provide component/range limits and independent calculations.If simulation is used,label it simulation,not physical evidence. Submit problem statement,principle,diagram,construction/working explanation,expected calculation,blank/actual evidence and limitations;do not claim unperformed results.
